behavior_constraints: Every completed or rejected connection writes a JSON line to /app/logs/access.log
Each entry has fields: ts (ISO 8601), service, client, endpoint ("" if none), bytes_in, bytes_out, duration_ms, result
result is one of: success, rejected_no_endpoint, rejected_rate_limit, rejected_conn_limit, retry_exhausted, idle_timeout
Log file and parent directory /app/logs are auto-created if missing
When access.log exceeds 1 MB it is renamed to access.log.1 (overwriting any existing .1) and a fresh access.log starts
Access logging uses a buffered channel / async writer goroutine and must not block connection handling
Access log buffer is fully flushed before graceful shutdown completes
get_access_log IPC command accepts optional service, last_n, result, min_duration_ms
get_access_log applies service/result/min_duration_ms filters first, then takes last_n entries
entities.summary: This round adds structured async JSON access logging with size-based rotation and flush-on-shutdown, plus get_access_log/get_access_stats IPC commands and meshctl access-log/access-stats CLI subcommands.

instruction_head:
Now add structured access logging to meshrouter.

Every completed or rejected connection must write a JSON line to `/app/logs/access.log`. Each entry has these fields:
- `ts`: ISO 8601 timestamp
- `service`: service name
- `client`: client address
- `endpoint`: selected endpoint address, or `""` if none was chosen
- `bytes_in`, `bytes_out`: byte counts for the connection
- `duration_ms`: milliseconds from accept to close
- `result`: one of `"success"`, `"rejected_no_endpoint"`, `"rejected_rate_l
